P.n: Shuri Castle (首里城)
P.w: Palace of the Ryūkyū Kingdom from 1429 to 1879 and the centrepiece of the UNESCO Gusuku Sites. Destroyed in 1945 and again by fire in 2019; the rebuilt Seiden (main hall) exterior is complete, its interior due to reopen on 23 November 2026.
P.k: UNESCO World Heritage gusuku; Seiden rebuild

P.n: Tamaudun Royal Mausoleum (玉陵)
P.w: Limestone tomb of the second Shō dynasty, built in 1501 under King Shō Shin and modelled on Shuri Castle, its balustrades carved with dragons, phoenixes and lions. A National Treasure as well as a UNESCO component.

P.n: Sonohyan-utaki Ishimon (園比屋武御嶽石門)
P.ad: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: Stone gate to the sacred grove behind it, where Ryūkyū kings prayed for safe journeys before leaving Shuri; a UNESCO component standing beside Shuri Castle Park.

P.n: Shikinaen Royal Garden (識名園)
P.w: The Ryūkyū royal family’s largest villa garden, built around a pond with jagged coral-limestone bridges two kilometres south of Shuri Castle; used to receive Chinese envoys and now a UNESCO component.

P.n: Naminoue Shrine (波上宮)
P.w: Okinawa’s ichinomiya (chief shrine), perched on a coral bluff above Naminoue Beach; long the place where fishermen and sailors prayed for a safe voyage.

P.n: Makishi Public Market (第一牧志公設市場)
P.w: Naha’s kitchen since 1950: 75 ground-floor stalls of spiny lobster, reef fish, pork and island produce, with upstairs restaurants that cook what you buy (mochiage). Reopened in a new building on 19 March 2023.

P.n: Sefa-utaki (斎場御嶽)
P.w: The holiest site of Ryūkyūan religion: a sacred grove of limestone clefts overlooking Kudaka Island, where the kingdom’s high priestess was invested. A UNESCO Gusuku component.

P.n: Nakagusuku Castle (中城城跡)
P.w: Best-preserved of the Ryūkyū castle ruins: six enclosures of curved limestone walls on a ridge above both coasts. UNESCO Gusuku component.

P.n: Nakijin Castle Ruins (今帰仁城跡)
P.w: Hilltop stronghold of the Hokuzan kingdom with long serpentine limestone walls. UNESCO Gusuku component.

P.n: Zakimi Castle Ruins (座喜味城跡)
P.w: Early-15th-century gusuku on a Yomitan hilltop, one of the five castle sites inscribed by UNESCO.

P.n: Katsuren Castle Ruins (勝連城跡)
P.w: Terraced gusuku ruins on the Katsuren peninsula, one of the five castle sites inscribed by UNESCO.

P.n: Okinawa Peace Memorial Park & Prefectural Peace Memorial Museum (平和祈念公園)
P.w: The main memorial to the Battle of Okinawa, on Mabuni Hill where the fighting ended in June 1945. The museum traces the lead-up, the battle and the rebuilding; outside, the Cornerstone of Peace lists every fallen soldier and civilian of every nationality.

P.n: Himeyuri Peace Museum (ひめゆり平和祈念資料館)
P.w: Museum beside the Himeyuri Monument, telling the story of the schoolgirls drafted as nurses into army cave hospitals in 1945, most of whom died. Opened 23 June 1989.

P.n: Former Japanese Navy Underground Headquarters (旧海軍司令部壕)
P.ad: Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan (Navy HQ park, south of Naha)
P.w: Several hundred metres of hand-dug tunnels and rooms that served as the Imperial Navy's command post in 1945; the walls still bear the shrapnel marks of the officers' last stand.

P.n: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium (沖縄美ら海水族館)
P.ad: Ocean Expo Park, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: Widely rated Japan's best aquarium, at the tip of the Motobu Peninsula. Its Kuroshio Tank — one of the largest in the world — holds whale sharks and manta rays.

P.n: Cape Manzamo (万座毛)
P.w: Grassy clifftop above the Onna coast with the elephant-trunk rock arch; one of the island's most-visited viewpoints.

P.n: Tokei Beach & Heart Rock, Kouri Island (ティーヌ浜)
P.w: The north-shore cove of 'Love Island' Kouri, reached by the long Kouri Ōhashi bridge, where the heart-shaped rock formation stands in the shallows.

P.n: Furuzamami Beach, Zamami Island (古座間味ビーチ)
P.w: Zamami's best beach, a 20-minute walk from the port: 'Kerama blue' water and reef straight off the sand; holds two Michelin Green Guide stars per the village.

P.n: Sunset Beach, Chatan (サンセットビーチ)
P.w: Artificial-bay beach beside Mihama American Village on the west coast, about 250 m of sand facing the sunset.

P.n: Zanpa Beach, Yomitan (残波ビーチ)
P.w: West-coast swimming beach beside Cape Zanpa, reached by airport limousine bus to the cape resort.

P.n: Okinawa World & Gyokusendo Cave (おきなわワールド 玉泉洞)
P.w: Culture park built over Gyokusendo, a 5 km limestone cave (850 m open) — the longest in the south and second-longest in Japan — with a craft village of old houses and a habu snake museum.

P.n: Yomitan Yachimun no Sato Pottery Village (やちむんの里)
P.w: Lane of red-tile workshops and climbing kilns founded after Living National Treasure Jiro Kinjo moved his studio here in 1972; around 45–50 potters, with shops selling cups, plates and shisa.

P.n: Cape Zanpa & Lighthouse (残波岬)
P.w: The main island's westernmost cape: 30 m cliffs and Okinawa's tallest lighthouse (31 m), a classic sunset spot, with a park and giant shisa statue.

P.n: Ōjima Island (奥武島)
P.w: Tiny bridge-linked fishing island off Nanjō, famous for cheap fresh-fish and seaweed tempura stands and its many cats.

P.n: Yonaha Maehama Beach (与那覇前浜)
P.w: Seven kilometres of white sand on Miyako's south-west tip, facing Kurima Island — the beach that usually tops rankings of Japan's best.

P.n: Kabira Bay (川平湾)
P.w: Turquoise-to-emerald bay on Ishigaki's north coast, a national Place of Scenic Beauty inside Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park; swimming is banned, so see it by glass-bottom boat over the black-pearl farms.

P.n: Tatami-ishi, Kume Island (畳石)
P.ad: Ōjima, Kumejima, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: About a thousand pentagonal and hexagonal andesite columns, each 1–1.5 m across, exposed at low tide on the south shore of Ōjima, bridged to Kume Island — a Miocene lava field that looks like tatami mats.

P.n: Hiji Falls (比地大滝)
P.ad: Kunigami Forest Park, Hiji, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: The main island's tallest waterfall (25.7 m), reached by a forest trail and suspension bridge through the Yanbaru subtropical woods from the Kunigami campground.

P.n: ASMUI Spiritual Hikes (former Daisekirinzan, 大石林山)
P.w: Trails through jagged limestone karst near Cape Hedo, a place of prayer for some 600 years — renamed ASMUI Spiritual Hikes.

P.n: Cape Hedo (辺戸岬)
P.w: The northernmost point of Okinawa Island: jagged limestone cliffs where the East China Sea meets the Pacific, with Yoron Island on the horizon and the Yanbaru-kuina observatory on the hill behind.

P.n: Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri pottery street (壺屋やちむん通り)
P.w: The Ryūkyū Kingdom's ceramics quarter: a 400 m stone-paved street between Kokusai-dōri and Route 330 lined with potteries, kilns and shops selling yachimun ware and shisa, with wheel-throwing classes.

P.n: Mihama American Village (美浜アメリカンビレッジ)
P.w: Reclaimed-land entertainment district with a Ferris wheel, Depot Island's colourful facades, US-style diners and boutiques — the clearest expression of Chatan's base-town melting pot.

P.n: Koza Gate 2 Street (コザ ゲート通り)
P.w: The street running to Kadena Air Base's Gate 2, Okinawa's live-music strip since the 1960s–70s: rock, blues and Latin bars alongside Okinawan folk; home of the November International Carnival.

P.n: Kaichū-dōro sea causeway (海中道路)
P.w: Five-kilometre road laid across turquoise shallows from the Katsuren Peninsula to Henza, then bridged on to Hamahiga, Miyagi and Ikei — the island-hop drive of central Okinawa.

P.n: Amamichu, Hamahiga Island (アマミチュー)
P.w: Rocky islet off 'God's Island' Hamahiga, revered as the tomb of Amamikiyo and Shinerikiyo, the creator deities of the Ryūkyū myths; reached on foot across a short causeway.

P.n: Ikei Beach, Ikei Island (伊計ビーチ)
P.w: Reef-sheltered beach on the farthest of the Kaichū-dōro islands, with some of the clearest water reachable by car from the main island.

P.n: Mount Omoto (於茂登岳)
P.w: At 525.5 m the highest peak in Okinawa Prefecture, rising from the Omoto range on Ishigaki's north; a forest trail climbs to views over Kabira and the reef. Paired with Kabira Bay as a national Place of Scenic Beauty.

P.n: Taketomi Island & village (竹富島)
P.w: Fifteen minutes by ferry from Ishigaki: a preserved Ryūkyū village of coral-stone walls, red-tiled houses and white-sand lanes travelled by water-buffalo cart — a national Important Preservation District since 1987 — ringed by Kondoi Beach.

P.n: Kurima Island & Kurima Ōhashi (来間島)
P.w: Small island reached by the 1.7 km Kurima Ōhashi from Miyako's south-west, with café stops and Nagamahama beach looking back across to Maehama.

P.n: Ikema Island & Ikema Ōhashi (池間島)
P.w: Fishing island off Miyako's northern tip, reached by the 1.4 km Ikema Ōhashi over shallow turquoise reef.

P.n: Tōri-ike, Shimoji Island (通り池)
P.w: Two collapsed-cave sinkholes in the coral of Shimoji's west coast — 75 m and 55 m across, linked to each other and the sea by an underwater cave — the 'dragon's eyes', a national Natural Monument and a celebrated cave dive.

P.n: Miyara Dunchi (宮良殿内)
P.w: Residence of a Ryūkyū-kingdom official built in 1819 in the style of Shuri samurai houses — an Important Cultural Property with a rock garden that is a Place of Scenic Beauty; still lived in, so viewed from outside.

P.n: Hoshizuna-no-hama star sand beach, Iriomote (星砂の浜)
P.ad: Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: Small north-shore Iriomote beach whose 'sand' includes millions of star-shaped foraminifera skeletons; snorkelling over the reef straight off the beach.

P.n: Yonekoyaki Shisa Park, Ishigaki (米子焼工房 シーサー園)
P.w: Roadside garden behind the Yonekoyaki pottery workshop crowded with giant, psychedelic, pop-art shisa lion-dog sculptures.

P.n: Hacksaw Ridge (Maeda Escarpment, 前田高地)
P.w: The Urasoe escarpment where medic Desmond Doss lowered wounded men down the cliff in May 1945; trails lead to Needle Rock and the Doss point above the city.

P.n: Kokusai-dōri (国際通り)
P.w: Naha's 1.6 km main street of shops, cafés, bars and awamori stores, rebuilt so fast after 1945 it was nicknamed the 'Miracle Mile'; the gateway to Makishi market, Tsuboya and the arcades, and the stage for the city's big festivals.

P.n: Kinjō-chō Ishidatami-michi stone-paved road (金城町石畳道)
P.w: About 300 m survive of the c.1522 limestone-paved royal road that ran south from Shuri Castle, winding steeply between old stone walls and red-tiled houses.

P.n: Okinawa Prefectural Museum & Art Museum (沖縄県立博物館・美術館)
P.w: The prefecture's flagship museum in Shintoshin: Ryūkyū history, nature and crafts from prehistory to the US era, with a modern Okinawan art wing.

P.n: Sakaemachi Market (栄町市場)
P.w: Showa-era covered market by Asato station: groceries by day, and after dark a warren of tiny bars and izakaya where locals drink on stools in the alleys.

P.n: Sunayama Beach (砂山ビーチ)
P.w: Cove reached over a tall sand dune 4 km north of Hirara, framed by a natural rock arch — one of Miyako's signature beaches.

P.n: Cape Higashi-hennazaki (東平安名崎)
P.w: A 2 km finger of land at Miyako's south-east tip, strewn with tsunami boulders, ending at a 1967 white lighthouse with a 320° ocean panorama.

P.n: Irabu Ōhashi Bridge (伊良部大橋)
P.w: Opened 31 January 2015: at 3,540 m Japan's longest toll-free bridge, arcing over turquoise shallows from Miyako to Irabu Island.

P.n: Valley of Gangala (ガンガラーの谷)
P.w: Collapsed-cave valley of banyan-draped limestone opposite Okinawa World, where remains linked to the 18,000-year-old Minatogawa people were found; visits by guided tour only.

P.n: Bise Fukugi Tree Road (備瀬のフクギ並木)
P.w: Kilometre of sandy lanes in Bise village tunnelled by centuries-old fukugi windbreak trees, five minutes from Churaumi; walk or cycle to Cape Bise.

P.n: Fukushū-en Garden (福州園)
P.w: Walled Chinese garden opened in 1992 for Naha's sister city Fuzhou, built with materials shipped from Fujian — pagoda over a waterfall, ponds and moon gates in old Kume, the Chinese scholars' quarter.

P.n: Hate-no-hama sandbar, Kume Island (ハテの浜)
P.ad: off eastern Kume Island, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: A 7 km ribbon of pure white sand bars in the open sea east of Kume Island, reached only by a 20-minute boat ride — no shade, no buildings, just reef and sky.

P.n: Nago Central Park / Nago Castle Park (名護城公園)
P.w: Hillside park on the old Nago gusuku site — the only place in Okinawa on Japan's list of 100 best cherry-blossom spots (deep-pink kanhi-zakura in late January) — with the Tenjo lookout over Nago Bay.

P.n: Nago Pineapple Park (ナゴパイナップルパーク)
P.w: Kitsch pineapple-themed park on Route 84 with self-driving pineapple carts through the plantation and tastings of pineapple everything.

P.n: DMM Kariyushi Aquarium (DMMかりゆし水族館)
P.ad: iias Okinawa Toyosaki, Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: Okinawa's second-largest aquarium, in the iias Toyosaki mall near the airport: projection and AR-enhanced tanks, penguins, and a walkway over a big shark-and-ray tank.

P.n: Ie Island & Mt Gusuku 'Tatchu' (伊江島 城山)
P.w: Flat island a 30-minute ferry from Motobu, dominated by the 172 m rock spire of Gusuku-yama ('Iejima Tatchu') — climb for views back to the Motobu Peninsula.

P.n: Sesoko Island & Sesoko Beach (瀬底島)
P.w: Small bridged island off Motobu with one of the main island area's clearest swimming beaches, facing Minna and Ie islands.

P.n: Mt Yaedake cherry-blossom road (八重岳桜の森公園)
P.w: Japan's first cherry blossoms of the year: about 7,000 deep-pink kanhi-zakura line a 4 km road up the main island's second-highest mountain, with a festival from mid-January.

P.n: Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Itoman (具志川城跡)
P.w: Gusuku perched on sea cliffs at the southern tip of the island, surrounded by sea on three sides — a National Historic Site with sweeping coastal views.

P.n: Itokazu Castle Ruins (糸数城跡)
P.w: Fourteenth-century gusuku at 180 m — the highest castle ruin in the south — its curved limestone walls built to guard Tamagusuku; views over the southern coast.

P.n: Tamagusuku Castle Ruins (玉城城跡)
P.w: The oldest castle on Okinawa Island, said to have been built by the creator goddess Amamikiyo; its arched gate in the natural rock frames the solstice sunrise. National Historic Site.

P.n: Chinen Castle Ruins (知念城跡)
P.w: Compact cliff-top gusuku with a pair of arched stone gates, believed to be the second-oldest castle in the Ryūkyūs; near the sacred Chinen-Ukka spring. National Historic Site.

P.n: Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Kume Island (具志川城跡)
P.w: Fifteenth-century gusuku on a cliff-bound headland in Kume Island's north-west, four low-walled enclosures above the East China Sea; National Historic Site since 1975.

P.n: Tsuboya Pottery Museum (那覇市立壺屋焼物博物館)
P.w: Municipal museum on Yachimun-dōri with some 7,000 pieces — from a 6,700-year-old shard through Ryūkyū-kingdom wares to today's masters — plus a preserved climbing kiln.

P.n: Tamatorizaki Observation Point, Ishigaki (玉取崎展望台)
P.w: Hilltop platform on Ishigaki's east coast looking over Cape Tamatori, Ibaruma Bay, the hilly Hirakubo peninsula and the reef.

P.n: Yubu Island water-buffalo crossing (由布島)
P.ad: Komi, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: Tiny island off Iriomote reached by water-buffalo cart across a shallow sandy strait, often to a sanshin song from the driver; a botanical garden and cafés on the island.

P.n: Iriomote Island jungle & mangroves (西表島)
P.w: Okinawa's second-largest island, about 90 % jungle and mangrove — part of the 2021 UNESCO natural World Heritage site and home of the critically endangered Iriomote cat; explored by river cruise and kayak (Urauchi River, Pinaisara Falls — the prefecture's tallest at 55 m).

P.n: Eef Beach, Kume Island (イーフビーチ)
P.w: Two kilometres of white sand on Kume's east coast, one of Japan's '100 Best Beaches', facing the lagoon and Hate-no-hama.

P.n: Ishigaki Yaima Village (石垣やいま村)
P.w: Open-air village of century-old Yaeyama houses (designated tangible cultural properties) beside a mangrove, with folk-song shows, crafts and the Anparu Shokudō serving Okinawa soba and jūshī.

P.n: Shinri-hama Beach, Kume Island (シンリ浜)
P.w: West-coast beach on Kume Island, the island's sunset spot.

P.n: Aragusuku Beach, Miyako (新城海岸)
P.w: East-coast reef beach where shallow, glass-clear water puts coral and tropical fish within a few strokes of the sand — Miyako's easy snorkel spot.

P.n: Cape Maeda & the Blue Cave (真栄田岬 青の洞窟)
P.w: Limestone cape on the Onna coast and the island's most popular snorkel and dive entry; swim or boat into the Blue Cave, where light through the sea floor turns the grotto luminous aquamarine.

P.n: Emerald Beach, Ocean Expo Park (エメラルドビーチ)
P.ad: Ocean Expo Park, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: Three-part beach inside Ocean Expo Park beside Churaumi, one of Japan's '100 best beaches'; free entry and parking, swimming April–October.

P.n: Kariyushi Beach (かりゆしビーチ)
P.w: Resort beach on Nago Bay's western shore with a long swimming season (March–October) and marine activities.

P.n: Okuma Beach (奥間ビーチ)
P.w: Year-round beach resort in Yanbaru, inside the World Natural Heritage north; long a favourite of base families.

P.n: Ginowan Tropical Beach (宜野湾トロピカルビーチ)
P.w: City beach by Ginowan's marina park, a long-time base-family BBQ and swim spot minutes from Naha.

P.n: Toyosaki Chura-Sun Beach (豊崎美らSUNビーチ)
P.w: Long artificial beach on the Toyosaki reclamation near the airport, with BBQ areas and planes overhead.

P.n: Araha Beach, Chatan (アラハビーチ)
P.w: 600 m of white sand in southern Chatan, quieter than Sunset Beach, with lifeguards, BBQ rental and water sports; swimming April–October.

P.n: Azama Sun Sun Beach (あざまサンサンビーチ)
P.w: Shallow family beach by Azama port (the ferry to Kudaka), fringed with lawns, with a beach house and reservable BBQ sets.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — the beach's wooden swing appears in the series; Nanjō named an 'Anime Pilgrimage 88' site (Ryukyu Shimpo entry-1580769) · Family beach

P.n: Mibaru Beach & glass-bottom boats (新原ビーチ)
P.w: Two kilometres of natural sand on the south-east coast, launch point for glass-bottom boats over the reef.

P.n: Toguchi Beach, Yomitan (渡具知ビーチ) — US landing beach
P.w: Beach at the mouth of the Hija River where US Marines came ashore on 1 April 1945; now a quiet park beach.

P.n: Aharen Beach, Tokashiki Island (阿波連ビーチ)
P.w: Tokashiki's main beach in the Kerama Islands National Park: a long curve of white sand and 'Kerama blue' reef water, with a campground nearby.

P.n: Cape Irizaki, Yonaguni — Japan's westernmost point (西崎)
P.w: Cliff-ringed cape at the west tip of Yonaguni, the last place in Japan to see the sunset: lighthouse, lookout and the 'westernmost point of Japan' monument; Taiwan, 107 km away, is visible on clear days.

P.n: Yonaguni Monument underwater formation (与那国島海底地形)
P.w: Terraced underwater rock formation found by a diver in 1986 off Yonaguni's south coast — natural or man-made is still debated; reached on dive and glass-bottom boat trips.

P.n: Nakanoshima Beach, Shimoji Island (中の島ビーチ)
P.w: High-walled bay on Shimoji's west coast whose coral starts metres from the sand — the best snorkelling beach on Irabu and Shimoji.

P.n: Yoshino Beach, Miyako (吉野海岸)
P.w: East-coast reef beach famous for snorkelling among dense coral and fish in knee-to-chest-deep water.

P.n: Mamoru-kun police-officer figures, Miyako (宮古島まもる君)
P.w: Life-size painted policeman figures posted at Miyako crossings by the traffic-safety association since the 1990s — now the island's cult mascot.

P.n: Benzaitendō & Enkaku-ji, Shuri (弁財天堂・円覚寺跡)
P.ad: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: Islet hall to the goddess of sea voyages in Enkan-chi pond, opposite the gate of Enkaku-ji — the royal family temple whose National Treasures were lost in 1945.

P.n: Nirai Kanai Bridge overlook (ニライカナイ橋)
P.w: A sweeping U-shaped road bridge that switchbacks down the Chinen hillside with the Pacific and Kudaka Island ahead — best seen from the tunnel-top viewpoint. It appears in the 2021 anime 'The Aquatope on White Sand', which earned Nanjō a place among the Anime Tourism Association's 88 anime pilgrimage sites.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — bridge shown in the series; Nanjō named an 'Anime Pilgrimage 88' site · Coastal bridge & viewpoint (anime pilgrimage)

P.n: Kouri Ōhashi Bridge & Kouri Island (古宇利大橋・古宇利島)
P.w: The 1,960 m toll-free bridge (2005) from Yagaji Island across emerald shallows to Kouri, the 'Island of Love' — one of Okinawa's signature drives, with beaches, Heart Rock and garlic-shrimp trucks at the far end.

P.n: Ama Beach, Zamami Island (阿真ビーチ)
P.w: The quieter of Zamami's two main beaches, on the southwest shore facing the uninhabited islets of Gahi and Agenashiku; sea turtles graze offshore.

P.n: Takatsukiyama Observatory, Zamami (高月山展望台)
P.w: Hilltop lookout over Zamami village, Furuzamami Beach and the scattered Kerama islands — the classic Kerama Blue panorama.

P.n: Pokémon Center Okinawa, Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom (ポケモンセンターオキナワ)
P.ad: Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom 1F, 1 Raikamu, Kitanakagusuku, Okinawa 901-2306, Japan
P.w: Okinawa's first Pokémon Center (opened 11 Aug 2022, Japan's 16th), themed on the island's nature: Pikachu and Arcanine greet you at the entrance, with Okinawa-only goods and a video zone. Pair it with a hunt for the prefecture's 16 Pokémon manhole 'Poké Lids'.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon — the prefecture's only Pokémon Center, with Okinawa-exclusive merchandise · Pokémon flagship store

P.n: Sueyoshi-gū Shrine & Sueyoshi Park (末吉宮)
P.w: One of the Eight Shrines of the Ryūkyū Kingdom, perched on a forested limestone ridge in Sueyoshi Park; a stone path climbs through jungle to the rebuilt hall — a quiet counterpoint to Shuri Castle.

P.n: Sōgen-ji Stone Gate (崇元寺石門)
P.w: The surviving stone gate of the Ryūkyū royal temple founded in 1527, where all who entered — even the king — had to dismount; the temple was destroyed in WWII but the gate was restored and has been an Important Cultural Property since 1972, fronting a small park.
P.k: Ryukyu royal temple gate (Important Cultural Property)

P.n: Ryūtan Pond, Shuri (龍潭)
P.ad: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: The 'Dragon Depths' pond below Shuri Castle, dug in 1427 under King Shō Hashi by the official Kaiki to entertain Chinese envoys; the classic reflection view of the castle walls.

P.n: Okinawa Karate Kaikan (沖縄空手会館)
P.w: The prefecture's home of karate, opened March 2017 on a 3.8 ha site near Naha Airport: a museum on the art's Okinawan origins, training dojo and the ceremonial Shureikan hall.

P.n: Michi-no-Eki Kadena observation deck (道の駅かでな)
P.w: Roadside station beside Kadena Air Base whose rooftop observation deck looks straight across the runway — the place locals and plane-spotters watch fighter jets take off and land; Mapple ranks it Okinawa's No. 3 michi-no-eki.

P.n: Ishigaki-jima Limestone Cave (石垣島鍾乳洞)
P.w: Japan's southernmost show cave: 3.2 km of limestone formed over some 200,000 years in southern Ishigaki, with a lit walkway through the formations.

P.n: Nishihama Beach, Hateruma Island (ニシ浜)
P.ad: Hateruma, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: The beach that gave its name to 'Hateruma Blue' — powder-white sand and impossibly saturated turquoise water on Japan's southernmost inhabited island; stay overnight for the star-field sky.

P.n: Sugar Road, Kohama Island (シュガーロード)
P.ad: Kohama, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
P.w: A straight lane through sugar-cane fields across Kohama Island, famous as a location of NHK's 2001 morning drama 'Chura-san'; cycle it from the port, then climb Ufudaki for a 360° view over the Yaeyama islands.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Chura-san (ちゅらさん, NHK asadora 2001) — the heroine's home island; Sugar Road is the drama's best-known location · Cane-field lane (TV drama location)

P.n: Aharen-enchi Viewpoint, Tokashiki (阿波連園地)
P.w: Headland park above Aharen on Tokashiki's south tip with views across the Kerama islands and the open sea; walking trails and lookout decks.

P.n: 17END, Shimoji Island (17エンド)
P.w: The shallows off the end of Shimoji Airport's runway 17, where a sandbar appears at low tide in remarkably clear turquoise water — about 15–20 minutes' drive from Miyako over the Irabu Bridge.

P.n: Cape Chinen Park (知念岬公園)
P.w: A grassy clifftop park at the tip of Chinen Cape, about 40 m above the sea, with a roughly 250-degree view over the reef toward Kudaka and Komaka islands, a short walk from Sefa-utaki. It is one of the settings of the 2021 anime 'The Aquatope on White Sand', the reason the Anime Tourism Association named Nanjō one of its '88 Anime Pilgrimage' sites.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — cape park shown in the series; Nanjō is an Anime Tourism '88' site · Cape viewpoint (anime pilgrimage)

P.n: Okitsura pilgrimage — Gushikawa, Uruma (沖ツラ聖地 具志川公民館・具志川ビーチ)
P.ad: 381 Gushikawa, Uruma, Okinawa, Japan (Gushikawa Community Hall 具志川公民館)
P.w: The residential Gushikawa district of Uruma is the main real-world setting of the anime 'Fall in Love with Okinawa Dialect' (沖ツラ). Gushikawa Beach appears in episode 2 and other walk-to-school scenes, and pilgrims start from the Gushikawa Community Hall, which hands out Uruma's official location map and has one of three Okitsura manhole covers (the others are at KIN Sunrise Beach and Michi-no-Eki Ginoza).
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Fall in Love with Okinawa Dialect (沖縄で好きになった子が方言すぎてツラすぎる / 沖ツラ, 2025 anime) — set in Gushikawa, Uruma; official city location map and collab manhole · Anime pilgrimage neighbourhood

P.n: Tomari International Cemetery (泊外人墓地)
P.ad: Tomari, Naha, Okinawa (north shore of Tomari Port)
P.w: A small walled cemetery on the north bank of Tomari Port holding about 22 foreigners from the 18th to early 20th centuries and some 300 post-war burials, with a monument to Commodore Perry's 1853 landing. Its oldest Western grave, of the British sailor 'WM HARES', is dated 1816.
P.k: Historic foreigners' cemetery & Perry landing monument

P.n: Naminoue Beach & Naminoue Umisora Park (波の上ビーチ・波の上うみそら公園)
P.w: Naha's only city beach, sitting below the cliff-top Naminoue Shrine, with free entry and swimming from mid-April to October. The adjoining Umisora Park's enclosed man-made bay is a favourite with people learning to dive.

P.n: Shuri Kannondō (Jigen-in) (首里観音堂 慈眼院)
P.w: A Rinzai Zen temple at the end of the old royal road out of Shuri, founded in 1618 by King Shō Kyū to give thanks for the safe return of his son (later King Shō Hō) from Satsuma captivity, and rebuilt after the Battle of Okinawa. Envoys bound for Edo prayed here for a safe voyage; free to visit.
P.k: Thousand-armed Kannon temple of the Ryūkyū kings

P.n: Kakazu Ridge — Kakazu Takadai Park (嘉数高台公園)
P.w: One of the fiercest battlefields of the 1945 Battle of Okinawa: US forces attacked Kakazu Ridge on 9 April 1945 and needed about 15 days to take it, with thousands dead on both sides. Today a hilltop park with a globe-shaped observation deck looking over Futenma Air Station and toward the Maeda Escarpment, plus surviving pillboxes.

P.n: Haebaru Army Hospital Shelter No. 20 (南風原陸軍病院壕 20号壕)
P.w: Hand-dug tunnel used as a ward of the Okinawa Army Hospital in 1945, where the Himeyuri student nurses were first assigned before the retreat south. Guided visits by appointment through the Haebaru Town Culture Center (¥300).

P.n: Minatogawa Stateside Town (港川ステイツサイドタウン)
P.w: A neighbourhood of 1950s–60s white single-storey 'foreign houses' built for US military families, now converted into cafés, bakeries, galleries and shops. Lanes are named after US states (Oregon, Arizona, Michigan, Kansas and more); about 5 minutes' walk from the Minatogawa bus stop.

P.n: Chibichiri Gama (チビチリガマ)
P.w: A natural cave near the US landing beaches where, in April 1945, 140 villagers sheltered as American forces approached and 83 died in a forced mass suicide. A memorial stands at the mouth; the cave itself is closed to entry out of respect, and memorial services are held each spring.

P.n: Nakamura House (中村家住宅)
P.w: A wealthy farmer's homestead built in the 1720s — the island's prime surviving example of early-modern Okinawan domestic architecture, with red-tiled roofs, a coral-stone wall and fukugi-tree windbreak; a National Important Cultural Property near Nakagusuku Castle.

P.n: Kudaka Island (久高島)
P.w: The 'island of the gods', 5.3 km off Cape Chinen: in Ryūkyū belief the creator goddess Amamikyo descended here, and kings once made pilgrimage to it. A slender 1.38 km² island reached by ferry from Azama port, explored by bicycle; some sacred groves are off-limits.

P.n: Urasoe Yōdore Royal Mausoleum & Urasoe Castle ruins (浦添ようどれ・浦添城跡)
P.w: Cliffside royal tombs carved under King Eiso in 1261, below the ridge of Urasoe Castle, seat of the early Chūzan kings. The ridge was a Japanese defensive line in 1945 and the tombs, badly damaged, were later restored; free entry and parking, ~15 min walk from Urasoe-Maeda monorail station.

P.n: Plaza House Shopping Center (プラザハウス ショッピングセンター)
P.w: Billed as Japan's first shopping center, opened in 1954 to serve officers and families of the nearby US Ryukyu Command HQ. Its mid-century three-storey atrium and single-storey arcade survive, now holding an international food market, cafés, bakeries, interiors stores and Okinawan crafts; it appears in the Agency for Cultural Affairs' survey of Okinawa's modern architecture.

P.n: Okinawa Zoo & Museum — Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni (沖縄こどもの国)
P.w: Japan's southernmost zoo and the only one in the prefecture, reopened in 2004 with a child-focused layout: Nature Land (the zoo, with Yanbaru and Okinawan native species), the three-storey hands-on Wonder Museum and a Children's Center with petting animals.

P.n: Pinaisara Falls, Iriomote (ピナイサーラの滝)
P.w: Okinawa Prefecture's highest waterfall — a 54 m drop on the Hinai River, reached by kayaking the Hinai mangroves and a jungle trail inside Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park.

P.n: Urauchi River & Mariyudu Falls, Iriomote (浦内川・マリユドゥの滝)
P.w: Okinawa's longest river: a boat cruise up the mangrove-lined Urauchi, then a jungle walk to Mariyudu Falls, a two-tier fall selected among Japan's 100 best waterfalls.
P.k: River cruise to a top-100 waterfall

P.n: Cape Hirakubo & lighthouse, Ishigaki (平久保崎)
P.w: The northern tip of Ishigaki's Hirakubo Peninsula; from the white lighthouse the Pacific lies on one side and the East China Sea on the other.

P.n: Cape Agarizaki, Yonaguni (東崎)
P.w: Cliff-top cape at Yonaguni's eastern end, grazed by Yonaguni horses, with views across to Iriomote on clear days.

P.n: Kondoi Beach, Taketomi Island (コンドイ浜)
P.w: Taketomi's west-coast swimming beach: white sand and a long, shallow emerald lagoon calm enough for small children; reached by rental bicycle from the village.

P.n: Neo Park Okinawa, Nago (ネオパークオキナワ)
P.w: Nago's municipal wildlife and botanical park (opened December 1992): about 100 species in free-roaming Africa, Amazon and Oceania zones, circled by a small light railway.

P.n: Gesashi Bay mangroves, Higashi (慶佐次湾のヒルギ林)
P.w: The second-largest mangrove forest on Okinawa's main island — about 10 ha along the Gesashi River estuary, explored by boardwalk or guided kayak.

P.n: Kinjō Tetsuo Archive at Shōfūen, Haebaru (金城哲夫資料館・松風苑)
P.ad: 1384 Tsukazan, Haebaru, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan (inside Shōfūen 松風苑)
P.w: The family home of Kinjō Tetsuo, the Okinawan scriptwriter who created Ultra Q, Ultraman and Ultraseven for Tsuburaya Productions, kept as a small free archive inside the Shōfūen ryōtei restaurant his family runs. The Anime Tourism Association picked it for its '88 Anime Pilgrimage Sites' in 2017. Visits are by reservation; the town lists hours as 11:30–17:00.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Ultraman / Ultra Q / Ultraseven — birthplace archive of creator-scriptwriter Kinjō Tetsuo; Anime Tourism '88' site (2017) · Ultraman creator's archive (pop-culture pilgrimage)

P.n: Nanjō City Regional Products Hall — Midori no Yakata Sēfā (南城市地域物産館 緑の館・セーファ)
P.w: The roadside products hall at the foot of Sēfa-utaki, with about 200 local souvenirs downstairs and a restaurant and café upstairs. It is the official Aquatope pilgrimage base: Nanjō keeps its Anime Tourism Association '88 Anime Pilgrimage' certification plate and goshuin-style memorial stamp here.
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (2021) — holds Nanjō's Anime Tourism '88' certification plate and pilgrimage stamp · Aquatope pilgrimage stamp & plate

P.n: Nishihara Kira Kira Beach (西原きらきらビーチ)
P.ad: Agarizaki, Nishihara, Nakagami District, Okinawa, Japan (Creed Nishihara Marine Park)
P.w: A 550 m man-made beach inside Creed Nishihara Marine Park on the east coast, with free entry and parking, sports fields, a barbecue area and beach-volleyball courts. It is the venue of the climactic tournament in the beach-volleyball anime 'Harukana Receive' (2018).
P.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Harukana Receive (はるかなレシーブ, 2018) — real venue of the series' final beach-volleyball tournament · Beach-volleyball anime setting

P.n: Sugar Loaf Hill (シュガーローフ / 安里52高地)
P.w: The low hill the US Marines called Sugar Loaf and the Japanese 'Asato Hill 52', locally Kerama-chiiji, was fought over by the 6th Marine Division and the Japanese 32nd Army in May 1945. Today it is the Asato reservoir park beside Omoromachi monorail station, with an inscribed marker amid the new city centre.
P.k: Battle of Okinawa hill in the middle of Shintoshin

P.n: Great Akagi Trees of Shuri Kinjō (首里金城の大アカギ)
P.w: A grove of six huge akagi (Bischofia) trees and one Ryūkyū hackberry behind the Uchikanagusuku shrine just off the Kinjō-chō stone road, designated a national Natural Monument in 1972; the largest is 5.2 m round and 13 m tall. No other such grove of giant akagi survives in a settled area of Okinawa.
P.k: National Natural Monument grove off the stone road

P.n: Kayauchi Banta cliff, Kunigami (茅打バンタ)
P.w: A ~100 m sheer cliff and lookout near the island's northern tip, inside Yanbaru National Park; the name ('banta' = cliff) comes from the tale that a bundle of thatch thrown over the edge was torn apart by the wind.

P.n: Senaga Island & Umikaji Terrace, Tomigusuku (瀬長島ウミカジテラス)
P.w: A small island ~600 m off the southern west coast and 1.5 km south of Naha Airport, returned by the US military in 1977; since summer 2015 its slope is lined with the white, Mediterranean-style shops and cafés of Umikaji Terrace, with planes landing overhead and sunset views.

P.n: Cape Kyan & the Peace Tower, Itoman (喜屋武岬)
P.w: The south-western tip of the main island, 10–20 m cliffs where the Pacific meets the East China Sea; this coast saw the last desperate fighting of the Battle of Okinawa, and the 1969 Peace Tower memorial stands at the point, inside Okinawa Senseki Quasi-National Park.

P.n: Todoroki Falls Park, Nago (轟の滝)
P.w: A roughly 28 m waterfall a five-minute drive inland from Route 58, designated a prefectural scenic spot; a small managed park (open 9–18, ¥200) with stream play and barbecue areas.

P.n: Shimashi Ōzato Castle Ruins, Nanjō (島添大里城跡)
P.ad: Ōzato, Ōzato, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan (Ōzato Castle Ruins Park)
P.w: A 14th-century gusuku on the eastern end of a ~150 m limestone ridge, seat of the Shimashi-Ōzato lords until Shō Hashi took it in 1402 on his way to unifying the Ryūkyū Kingdom; designated a National Historic Site in 2012.

P.n: Uegusuku Castle Ruins, Kume Island (宇江城城跡)
P.w: Gusuku ruins on the 310 m summit of Uegusuku-dake — the highest castle site in Okinawa Prefecture — with a 360-degree view over almost the whole of Kume Island. Free. Designated a National Historic Site in 2009.

P.n: Hiyajō Banta viewpoint, Kume Island (比屋定バンタ)
P.w: Lookout on the edge of a 200 m sea cliff on Kume's north coast, looking out to the Hate-no-hama sandbar and, on clear days, the Kerama Islands. Free.

P.n: Mīfugā rock, Kume Island (ミーフガー)
P.w: Strange split sea-rock on Kume's north-west shore known as the 'female rock'; by local legend, childless women who pray here are blessed with children.

P.n: Toguchi-no-hama Beach, Irabu Island (渡口の浜)
P.w: An 800 m gently curving arc of fine white sand on south-west Irabu, renowned across Okinawa for its powdery sand and clear water, looking across to Miyako and Kurima islands; counted among Irabu's finest beaches.

P.n: Takanazaki & Japan's Southernmost Point Monument, Hateruma (高那崎・日本最南端の碑)
P.ad: Hateruma Island, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa (south tip; ~10 min by car from Hateruma port)
P.w: Kilometre-long limestone cliffs at the southern tip of Hateruma, Japan's southernmost inhabited island, where a monument to the southernmost point (erected 1970) stands beside Taketomi Town's peace monument and a path of stones from every prefecture.

F.n: Kishimoto Shokudo (きしもと食堂)
F.ad: near Motobu Municipal Market, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Soba shop founded in 1905 near the Motobu market: flat noodles still made with tree-ash lye water, in a light bonito-and-soy broth with thick boneless rib, kamaboko and island onion.

F.n: King Tacos Kin (キングタコス 金武本店)
F.w: The taco-rice institution in downtown Kin: seasoned taco meat, cheese, lettuce and tomato over rice — the dish created in Kin in 1984 by Matsuzo Gibo of Parlor Senri.

F.n: Gabusoka Shokudo Honten (我部祖河食堂 本店)
F.w: Founded in 1966 and billed as the birthplace of soki soba: the founder, then a butcher, simmered unsold spare ribs for hours and laid them on soba. House-made wavy noodles, punchy pork-bone broth.

F.n: Yanbaru Soba (山原そば)
F.ad: 70-1 Izumi, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: The queue-before-opening star of the Motobu 'soba road' (Route 84): a mellow bonito-and-pork broth unchanged for four decades, soki or three-layer pork on top; closes when the noodles run out.

F.n: Mexico, Chatan (タコス専門店 メキシコ)
F.w: Taco-only shop serving since 1977 — one of the island's most famous taco joints, crisp shells stuffed with seasoned beef in the style US servicemen brought to Okinawa.

F.n: Zuisen Distillery (瑞泉酒造)
F.w: Shuri awamori maker descended from the distillers who supplied the royal court; free tour of the stills and fermentation tanks, a look into the kusu ageing cellar and a tasting of Zuisen and Omoro.

F.n: Mikasa Matsuyama (三笠 松山店)
F.w: Round-the-clock homestyle shokudō near the Prefectural Office: gōyā champurū, spam and egg, and the house 'chanpon' — Okinawa's stir-fry-on-rice take — in a room that feels like grandma's kitchen.

F.n: Jack's Steak House (ジャッキーステーキハウス)
F.w: Opened in 1953 under the US occupation and still displaying its 'A-sign' — the US-military approval certificate; the benchmark of Okinawa's post-war steak culture, open till 1 a.m.

F.n: Yūnangi (ゆうなんぎい)
F.w: Family-run Okinawan restaurant on a side street off Kokusai-dōri, serving home cooking since 1970 under US administration — hard to get a seat, rated among the best Okinawan food in Naha.

F.n: Hamaya Soba (そば専門店 浜屋)
F.w: Soba specialist by the Sunabe seawall, a local and tourist favourite for its soft-boned cartilage soki in a clean, salt-seasoned broth.

F.n: Charlie's Tacos, Koza (チャーリー多幸寿)
F.w: Koza taco counter a short walk from Kadena's Gate 2 where locals, mainlanders and Americans have queued for more than 60 years — one of the A-sign-era base-town originals.

F.n: Kojasobaya (古謝そば屋)
F.w: Miyako soba shop founded in 1932 by the Koja noodle-making family, under a red-tile roof; lunchtime queues for Miyako soba, soki soba and curry soba.

F.n: Rakuen no Kajitsu, Kurima Island (楽園の果実)
F.w: Farm café on Kurima Island using its own tree-ripened mango (July–Aug) and dragon fruit (July–Oct) in parfaits and sweets, plus a Miyako-beef rice bowl.

F.n: Doug's Burger Miyakojima (ダグズ・バーガー)
F.w: Island burger joint using 100 % Miyako-island beef, plus a burger of local yellow-fin tuna — the Miyako take on Okinawa's American-era burger culture.

F.n: Hamabe no Chaya (浜辺の茶屋)
F.w: Founded in 1994 as Okinawa's first seaside café: a driftwood lodge on a shallow beach whose window counter sits right over the water at high tide.

F.n: Café Kurukuma (カフェくるくま)
F.w: Cliff-top Asian-herb restaurant café with a terrace and herb-garden promenade looking out over the Pacific.

F.n: Shuri Soba (首里そば)
F.w: Lunch-only Shuri shop carrying on the noodle technique of a vanished Shuri original: unbleached flour pressed and rested over two days, a single soba on the menu, queues from before opening and sold out early.

F.n: Ryūkyū Cuisine Mie (琉球料理 美榮)
F.w: Founded in 1958 to reproduce the Ryūkyū royal court cuisine of Shō Junnan, gourmet son of the last king, in a wooden two-storey ryōtei behind a formal gate in Kumoji.

F.n: Izumi Soba (伊豆味そば)
F.ad: Izumi, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Soba stop on the Route 84 'soba road' through Izumi, picked in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers as one of the north's best.

F.n: Arayama Soba (新山そば)
F.w: Nago soba house founded in 1925 and run by the third generation: thick, springy flat noodles in an agu-pork-bone and bonito broth; profiled by the Okinawa Times as a century-old favourite.

F.n: Tamakaya Soba Honten (そば処 玉家 本店)
F.w: Soba specialist prized for the balance of broth, noodles and toppings — first on the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll's southern list.

F.n: Suunumee (すーぬめぇ)
F.w: Soba in an old Okinawan house in Kokuba; the 'special' piles on soki, belly and the owner's prized tebichi. On the Okinawa Times 2023 reader-poll list.

F.n: Nemu Isa (根夢 伊佐店)
F.w: Ginowan soba shop whose broth blends separately made bonito and pork-bone stocks at seven to three; picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll's central list.

F.n: Misato Soba (美里そば)
F.w: Okinawa City soba specialist with a layered chicken, pork-bone and bonito broth; on both the Okinawa Times 2023 central poll list and KozaWeb's city top ten.

F.n: Komehachi Soba (米八そば)
F.w: Awase soba shop known for its 'triathlon' bowl topped with all three Okinawan pork cuts; on the Okinawa Times 2023 central list and KozaWeb's top ten.

F.n: Kinatsuyu (八重山そば処 来夏世)
F.w: Old-house Yaeyama-soba specialist in Ishigaki town keeping the simple, light traditional flavour; the soba set with jūshī rice draws a noon queue. 'The royal road of Yaeyama soba' in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll.

F.n: Nakayoshi Shokudō, Ishigaki (なかよし食堂)
F.w: Comfort-food Yaeyama soba diner in Ishigaki, on the Okinawa Times 2023 reader-poll list and Mapple's Ishigaki soba round-up.

F.n: Sennichi (千日)
F.w: Naha's classic zenzai parlour near Naminoue Shrine, in business since the 1950s (the founders' Yafune Shokudo, then 'Sennichi' in Kume from 1962). Order the Okinawa zenzai: plump, slow-stewed beans under a triangle of hand-shaved ice.

F.n: A&W Makiminato (A&W 牧港店)
F.w: A&W came to Okinawa in 1963, years before mainland Japan — the 24-hour Makiminato drive-in on Route 58 is the chain's Okinawa flagship. Root beer in a frosted mug, curly fries and a burger is a rite of passage.

F.n: Steakhouse 88 Tsuji Honten (ステーキハウス88 辻本店)
F.w: Flagship of the Steakhouse 88 chain, descended from 'CLUB88', an A-sign restaurant licensed for US personnel in 1955. Neon diner room, 20-plus steak cuts, open till 1 am — the classic Okinawan 'shime' (end-of-night) steak.

F.n: Nakamura Soba (なかむらそば)
F.w: Roadside soba house near Manza Beach: preservative-free house noodles, a light but bonito-rich broth and pork belly that falls apart at a touch; the aasa soba works sea lettuce into both noodles and topping.

F.n: OKINAWA SOBA EIBUN
F.w: A newer-generation Naha soba shop that made both the Okinawa Times 900-reader noodle poll and Okinawa Traveler's five soba shops locals recommend with confidence.

F.n: Yagiya (屋宜家)
F.ad: 1172 Ōgan, Yaese, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Soba served in a registered cultural-property red-tiled house; choose classic, soy-milk or seaweed noodles in a light but deep bonito broth.

F.n: Nanbu Soba (南部そば)
F.ad: Southern Okinawa main island, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Southern soba shop picked both in the Okinawa Times 2023 noodle-lovers' poll (south edition) and by Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five.

F.n: Ufuya (百年古家 大家)
F.w: A century-old Okinawan farmhouse compound in the hills above Nago serving soki soba and agu pork; one of Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five and on Stars and Stripes' soba trail.

F.n: Arakaki Zenzai-ya (新垣ぜんざい屋)
F.w: Motobu's half-century-old zenzai shop that does exactly one thing: sweet stewed red kidney beans buried under a peak of shaved ice, bought with a ticket from the door.

F.n: Shima-jikan, Onna (沖縄料理の店 島時間)
F.w: Onna village Okinawan kitchen certified by Okinawa Prefecture as a 'restaurant where you can taste Ryukyu cuisine' and picked in Okinawa Traveler's soba round-up.

F.n: Inaka Ryōri no Mise Kura, Miyako (田舎料理の店 蔵)
F.w: Country-cooking izakaya in Hirara using island miso in champuru and rafute; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine and a Mapple guidebook pick.

F.n: Urizun (古酒と琉球料理 うりずん)
F.w: Opened 15 August 1972 by gathering bottles from every awamori distillery in Okinawa — the bar that brought awamori back to the people. Order duru-ten, the fried taro croquette Okinawa Times traces to this kitchen, and a flight of kūsu (aged awamori).

F.n: Irabu Soba Kame (伊良部そば かめ)
F.w: Irabu Island's soba stop, where the bonito hits you first; reached over the Irabu Bridge and named in both Okinawa Times' Miyako soba coverage and Mapple's Miyako-soba top ten.

F.n: Maruyoshi Shokudō (丸吉食堂)
F.w: Out in Gusukube, a family shokudō serving the owner's mother's Miyako soba: pork-bone broth perfumed with garlic and big soki ribs.

F.n: Yamato Shokudō (大和食堂)
F.w: Hirara regulars' shop serving the same plain, honest Miyako soba for some forty years.

F.n: Minato Shokudō, Miyako (みなと食堂)
F.w: Harbour-side shokudō near Sunayama whose house noodles are kneaded with aosa seaweed and served in a broth from bonito trimmings — a taste found only here.

F.n: Jinku-ya (じんく屋)
F.w: Counter run by Kusamatsu Seimen, one of Miyako's two big noodle makers: chewy fresh noodles, simple bonito soup.

F.n: Ishigaki-gyū Sumibi Yakiniku Yamamoto (石垣牛 炭火焼肉 やまもと)
F.w: The Ishigaki-beef yakiniku house locals queue for: buying whole animals means rare cuts on the board, grilled over charcoal; opens at 17:00 and closes when the meat runs out.

F.n: Shima no Ushi Ishigaki-ya (島のうし 石垣屋)
F.w: A more polished Ishigaki-beef room with private booths, picked by both of Japan's big guidebook series for island black wagyu.

F.n: Kimi Shokudō, Ishigaki (キミ食堂)
F.w: Ishigaki town shokudō famous for its miso-broth take on Yaeyama soba — a noodle-lovers' poll pick and one of Rurubu's 'creative' soba bowls.

F.n: Shiraho Shokudō (白保食堂)
F.w: Village shokudō in Shiraho on Ishigaki's east coast with a long menu from island dishes to yōshoku; the Yaeyama soba is the best seller.

F.n: Dachibin Naha Kumoji (沖縄居酒屋 抱瓶 那覇久茂地店)
F.w: The Naha outpost of an Okinawan izakaya that made its name in Tokyo, in a Shōwa-era wooden house; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine.

F.n: Orion Happy Park — Orion Beer Nago Brewery (オリオンハッピーパーク)
F.w: Okinawa's own beer since 1957: the Nago plant's tour ends with a tasting of just-brewed Orion Draft; shop, restaurant and a small history gallery.

F.n: Chatan Harbor Brewery & Restaurant (チャタンハーバーブルワリー)
F.w: Seafront brewpub a few minutes from American Village brewing five year-round beers on site, with a terrace over the East China Sea at sunset.

F.n: Helios Distillery (ヘリオス酒造)
F.w: Founded as a rum distiller in 1961 and brewing Okinawa's pioneering craft beer since 1996; the free tour shows 2,600 barrels of aging awamori stacked to the roof.

F.n: Ganso Nakamoto Tempura, Ōjima (元祖中本てんぷら店)
F.w: The queue-every-day tempura stand facing Ōjima fishing port, attached to a fish shop: thick-battered Okinawan tempura of fish, squid, mozuku seaweed and vegetables, eaten hot by the sea.

F.n: Tomigusuku Taco Rice (豊見城タコライス)
F.w: A new-wave taco rice: spiced meat, three cheeses, corn tortilla and a torched soki rib on top.

F.n: Nantō Shokurakuen, Kume Island (南島食楽園)
F.w: Big open izakaya by Eef Beach built around Kume's own produce: kuruma prawns raised in deep-ocean water, sea grapes, island red chicken, grouper and octopus, from Okinawan plates to nigiri.

F.n: Sukeroku Kamaboko, Kume Island (助ろく)
F.w: Kume's fish-cake maker, carrying on a 60-year-old craft: chewy island kamaboko flavoured with kuruma prawn, mozuku or squid ink — a classic island snack.

F.n: Sobadokoro Takenoko, Taketomi (そば処 竹の子)
F.ad: Taketomi Village, Taketomi Island, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Taketomi's most popular eating house, around forty years old, ladling the previous generation's Yaeyama soba in the red-tile village.

F.n: Tamagusuku Coffee Roasters (タマグスクコーヒー)
F.w: Ten-seat roaster-café off Kokusai-dōri often called the island's best cup: the owner asks what you like, then drips light-to-dark single origins one cup at a time.

F.n: Coffee Yatai Hibari-ya (珈琲屋台 ひばり屋)
F.w: An open-air coffee stall tucked into a leafy back alley near Makishi Station — ground-to-order hand drip and a famous deep-roast iced coffee on mismatched chairs.

F.n: rokkan COFFEE SHURI (ロッカン コーヒー シュリ)
F.w: Second shop (Oct 2023) of Naha roaster rokkan COFFEE CREATORS, opening at 6 am near Shuri Castle — a 'sixth sense' coffee before the castle crowds.

F.n: Tacos Café Tacoloco, Chatan (タコスカフェ タコロコ)
F.w: American Village taquería making properly Mexican tacos — spices shipped from Mexico — a counterpoint to Okinawa's crunchy-shell post-war tacos.

F.n: Itoman Fishermen's Co-op Osakana Center, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (糸満漁協 お魚センター)
F.w: Eleven fishmongers run by the Itoman fishermen's co-op inside Japan's southernmost roadside station: choose fish for a kaisendon, nigiri, fish soup or Okinawan tempura and eat on the spot, 10:00–19:00.

F.n: Mendokoro Tiandaa (麺処 てぃあんだー)
F.w: Cult Naha soba shop known for house-made noodles; the fūchibā soba arrives fragrant with Okinawan mugwort. In both Okinawa Traveler's soba feature and Mapple's Okinawa-soba round-up.

F.n: Sobaya Yoshiko, Motobu (そば屋よしこ)
F.w: One of the stars of Motobu's 'soba highway' (Prefectural Route 84, 20-plus soba shops): come for the meltingly braised tebichi on a pork-bonito-kombu broth.

F.n: Teppanyaki Steak House Shiki, Sonoda Honten (ステーキハウス四季 園田本店)
F.w: A Koza teppanyaki steak house running for close to half a century in the post-war steak heartland by Kadena; chefs sear the steak on the iron in front of you.

F.n: Kaizoku Kōbō, Okinawa Zoo & Museum (こどもの国レストラン 海族工房)
F.ad: Okinawa Zoo & Museum (Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni), Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: The zoo's ground-floor restaurant is no afterthought: prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine and picked by Okinawa City's tourism portal for its 'A-lunch', the post-war diner combo plate.

F.n: Highway Drive-In Restaurant, Okinawa City (ハイウェイ食堂)
F.w: Opened in 1972 by a US Army cook as an A-sign establishment and seemingly frozen in time since: huge diner plates, low prices, fast service, open till 2 am on Route 75.

F.n: Blue Seal Makiminato Honten (ブルーシール 牧港本店)
F.w: 'Born in America, raised in Okinawa': Blue Seal started in 1948 supplying the US bases and moved to this Makiminato drive-in in 1963. The flagship was rebuilt and reopened in 2024 to a 400-person queue — order beni-imo or salt-chinsukō.

F.n: Onna no Eki Nakayukui Ichiba (おんなの駅 なかゆくい市場)
F.w: West-coast roadside market that every drive north stops at: island produce, snack stalls frying sata andagi (brown sugar, beni-imo and more), and Ryu-pin's mountainous tropical-fruit kakigōri.

F.n: Michi-no-Eki Kyoda — Yanbaru Bussan Center (道の駅許田)
F.w: The roadside station at the end of the Okinawa Expressway, gateway to Yanbaru: produce from the twelve northern towns and a takeout row famous for hot Okinawan tempura and tacos. Renewed in 2021.

F.n: Awamori to Okinawa Ryōri Gōya, Miyako (泡盛と沖縄料理 郷家)
F.w: Hirara's classic shimauta izakaya: Miyako's own awamori brands, island home cooking, and nightly sanshin folk-song sets that end with the whole room dancing kachāshī.

F.n: RICCO gelato, Miyako (リッコジェラート)
F.w: Italian-trained gelato maker in Hirara churning Miyako's own mangoes, fruits and even island salt and vegetables into some thirty flavours.

F.n: Shima Café Tunkaraya, Miyako (島cafe とぅんからや)
F.w: Hilltop café in southern Miyako looking over the sea, cooking 'made in Miyako' lunches and fruit-heavy desserts.

F.n: Ishigaki-jima Milmil Honpo (石垣島ミルミル本舗)
F.w: Dairy-farm gelato stand on a hill above the sea west of Ishigaki town; the plain milk flavour is the best seller. Open until sunset.

F.n: Benriya Yulinglong, Sakaemachi (べんり屋 玉玲瓏)
F.w: The pioneer of Sakaemachi market's night drinking: when the stalls shutter, tables fill the alley for its hand-made gyōza. Both Rurubu and Mapple name it first among the market's after-dark haunts.

F.n: Nakamura-ya, Kumoji (海産物料理とあわもりの店 なかむら家)
F.w: Seafood-and-awamori izakaya in Kumoji where regulars come for whatever the boats brought in — island fish sashimi and simmered fish, washed down with awamori.

F.n: Karakara to Chibugwā (カラカラとちぶぐゎ〜)
F.ad: Yamako 2nd Bldg 1F, 3-15-15 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Naha's awamori-specialist bar: bottles from every distillery in the prefecture and aged kūsu past thirty years, with three awamori sommeliers to steer you; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine.

F.n: Kozakura (小桜)
F.w: A seventy-year-old koryōriya off Kokusai-dōri, believed to be the oldest surviving restaurant of its era in Naha; the third-generation owner keeps both old and new Okinawan dishes on the menu.

F.n: oHacorté Minatogawa Honten (オハコルテ 港川本店)
F.w: The fruit-tart shop (founded 2009) that made Minatogawa's 'Stateside Town' — some thirty shops and cafés in converted 1950s US military housing — a destination; glossy seasonal tarts in a little white house.

F.n: Yama no Chaya Rakusui, Nanjō (山の茶屋 楽水)
F.w: A café built into the rock above Hyakuna beach, sister to Hamabe no Chaya below — slow island lunches with a sea view through the trees.

F.n: Pizza Kissa Kajinhō, Motobu (ピザ喫茶 花人逢)
F.w: Red-tiled old-house café on a hilltop above Motobu serving the same home-made pizza for a quarter-century; on clear days Ie-jima, Sesoko and Minna float on the horizon.

F.n: Yachimun Kissa Shīsā-en, Motobu (やちむん喫茶 シーサー園)
F.w: A red-roofed Okinawan farmhouse swallowed by subtropical forest, with more than a hundred local potters' shīsā lions perched on roofs and walls around the tables.

F.n: Cafe ichara, Motobu (カフェ イチャラ)
F.w: A Motobu forest café picked by Rurubu, Mapple and Okinawa Traveler's 'sea or forest?' round-up of northern cafés.

F.n: Cafe Yabusachi, Nanjō (カフェ やぶさち)
F.w: Glass-fronted café on the Nanjō coast looking straight out over the Pacific — part of the trio of southern sea-view cafés with Hamabe no Chaya and Rakusui.

F.n: Shima Ryōri Izakaya Adan-tei, Ishigaki (島料理居酒屋 あだん亭)
F.w: Ishigaki town izakaya cooking genuinely Yaeyaman dishes from island produce — try the champuru of adan (screw-pine) shoots — and the only Yaeyama restaurant on the prefecture's Ryukyu-cuisine certified list.

F.n: Michi-no-Eki Yuiyui Kunigami (道の駅 ゆいゆい国頭)
F.w: The Yanbaru roadside station that gathers Kunigami village's food: Oku-grown green tea, karagi tea and the local Kunigami doughnuts — the last big food stop before Cape Hedo.

F.n: Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki (道の駅 豊崎)
F.w: The roadside station closest to Naha Airport, stocked with Tomigusuku's mango products and island produce — a last-stop for food souvenirs.

F.n: Takaesu Soba, Urasoe (高江洲そば)
F.w: An Urasoe institution counted among the 'traditional royal-road' soba shops by Rurubu and voted into the Okinawa Times noodle-lovers' central-region list.

F.n: Kingetsu Soba Yomitan Honten (金月そば 読谷本店)
F.w: Yomitan soba house on both Okinawa Traveler's area-by-area soba list and Rurubu's 16 best Okinawa-soba shops.

F.n: Sachichan Soba (幸っちゃんそば)
F.w: A northern soba shop picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 noodle-lovers' poll (north edition) and Rurubu's 16 'famous & characterful' soba shops.

F.n: Chadokoro Makabe Chinā, Itoman (茶処 真壁ちなー)
F.w: Soba and herb tea served in a red-tiled, stone-walled homestead whose house and grounds are a national Registered Tangible Cultural Property — the old southern-village Okinawa landscape intact.

F.n: Keishoku no Mise Ruby, Tomari (軽食の店ルビー)
F.w: Sixty-plus-year-old Tomari diner whose name belies mountainous portions: some 80 dishes from champuru to loco moco, but half the room orders the C-lunch. Namie Amuro used to drop in after dance practice.

F.n: Ayagu Shokudō, Shuri — CLOSED
F.w: Shuri's 'tasty, fast, cheap' shokudō, opened 1979 with a menu that once topped 100 dishes, closed at the end of October 2023 after 44 years when rising costs made it unsustainable. Kept on the map as a closed landmark of Okinawan shokudō culture — do not travel for it.

F.n: Ichigin Shokudō, Kumoji — CLOSED
F.w: Downtown Naha's 24-hour Okinawan diner, a C-lunch favourite, closed on 23 January after staff shortages and soaring costs (Okinawa Times). Listed as closed — do not travel for it.

F.n: Yanbaru Shokudō, Naha (やんばる食堂)
F.ad: In front of Okinawa University, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Opened 1974 opposite Okinawa University and still feeding students from a menu of more than eighty dishes — an Okinawan 'mother's cooking' shokudō in both Rurubu's and Okinawa Traveler's local-diner picks.

F.n: Oshokujidokoro Mikado, Naha (お食事処 みかど)
F.w: A Route 58 shokudō where Okinawan mothers cook the island's everyday dishes — champuru, soups, chanpon rice — fast and cheap.

F.n: Kaiyō Shokudō, Tomigusuku (海洋食堂)
F.w: Tomigusuku shokudō famous for yushi-dōfu, soft just-made island tofu carried over from the adjoining tofu works and served in soup or soba.

F.n: Mori no Kenja, Ishigaki (森の賢者)
F.w: Small Ishigaki-town kitchen cooking island vegetables, fish and Ishigaki beef without chemical seasonings, with awamori, sake and more than 45 home-made fruit and herb liqueurs; book ahead.

F.n: Maguro Senmon Izakaya Hitoshi, Ishigantō (まぐろ専門居酒屋 ひとし 石敢當店)
F.w: Ishigaki's famous tuna izakaya, packed with locals and visitors alike for heaped plates of just-landed island tuna; book or queue at 16:30.

F.n: KITCHEN inaba, Iriomote (キッチン イナバ)
F.ad: 742-6 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Iriomote's island-food kitchen near Uehara port: rare local ingredients — irabu sea-snake soup, gazami crab, Ryukyu wild boar in season — alongside traditional and Western-style plates, with jungle-green mountains in the windows.

F.n: Shima Gourmet ROCO, Iriomote (島ぐるめ ROCO)
F.ad: 58 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Uehara dining room cooking Iriomote's sea and mountain catch — grilled crab, sashimi salad, squid-ink rice croquettes and grouper simmered in island salt.

F.n: Umi-no-Eki Ayahashi-kan, Kaichū-dōro (海の駅 あやはし館)
F.w: The 'sea station' halfway along the 5 km Kaichū-dōro causeway: local produce and the Kaichū Chaya restaurant upstairs serving soki soba and taco rice over the shallows.

F.n: Nuchi Māsu Salt Factory, Miyagi Island (ぬちまーす観光製塩ファクトリー)
F.w: Clifftop salt works across the Kaichū-dōro on Miyagi Island, where a patented spray-drying method snows mineral-rich salt inside the factory; free 10-minute tours every 20 minutes, a sea-view restaurant and shop.

F.n: Awamori Masahiro Gallery, Itoman (泡盛まさひろギャラリー)
F.w: Gallery-shop of Masahiro Distillery (founded 1883): watch the production line through glass, browse displays on awamori's history and taste for free.

F.n: Uema Kashiten Factory — Suppaiman (上間菓子店 工場見学)
F.w: Free factory tour of the maker of Suppaiman, Okinawa's cult dried-plum snack and its mascot; watch the plums and candies being made (video only on Saturdays).

F.n: Restaurant Marumi-ya, Zamami (レストラン まるみ屋)
F.ad: Zamami village, Zamami Island, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Five minutes from Zamami port: hearty daily set lunches built on island produce — mozuku seaweed champuru and house-made jīmāmi peanut tofu are the favourites.

F.n: Karaoke Izakaya Marine Box, Tokashiki (カラオケ居酒屋マリンボックス)
F.w: The port-side all-rounder of Tokashiki village: an A-lunch plate at midday, then island izakaya dishes and karaoke until midnight.

F.n: Hanagasa Shokudō (花笠食堂)
F.w: A popular old-style shokudō off the Heiwa-dōri arcade serving Okinawan home cooking as set meals: pick white, brown or red (sekihan) rice and one of five soups including inamuruchi and nakami-jiru. Its sweet house iced tea is famous enough to have been sold in cartons.

F.n: Uchinā Chaya Buku-Buku, Tsuboya (うちなー茶屋 ぶくぶく)
F.w: A small teahouse on Tsuboya's pottery street that whips bukubuku-cha, the frothy rice-and-jasmine tea with Ryūkyū-dynasty roots, in front of you. Named in Visit Okinawa's Naha guide.

F.n: COFFEE potohoto, Sakaemachi (コーヒー ポトホト)
F.w: A tiny self-roasting coffee stand inside the post-war Sakaemachi Market, whose owner placed 5th at the 2014 Japan Coffee Roasting Championship per Rurubu. Mapple names it among Sakaemachi's recommended stops.

F.n: Yagi Ryōri Misaki, Sakaemachi (山羊料理 美咲)
F.w: A goat-meat specialist in the Sakaemachi Market alleys — goat is a traditional Okinawan celebration food. Featured by both Stars and Stripes' Sakaemachi guide and Mapple's Sakaemachi restaurant roundup.

F.n: Sangoza Kitchen (さんご座キッチン)
F.w: A café-bar inside Sakurazaka Gekijō, Naha's historic art-house cinema, five minutes from the Heiwa-dōri market arcade, with a selection of awamori, beer, wine and sake. Mapple lists it among the Kokusai-dōri area's cheap-drinking (senbero) stops.

F.n: Ryūkyū Kashidokoro Ryūgū, Heiwa-dōri (琉球菓子処 琉宮 平和通り店)
F.w: A sātā andāgī specialist on the Heiwa-dōri market arcade off Kokusai-dōri, frying its own flour blend in plain, brown-sugar, coconut and black-sesame flavours. Stars and Stripes also singles out its big, colourful 'Yumeiro' zenzai shaved ice.

F.n: Okinawa Soba Naha-tei (沖縄そば 那覇亭)
F.w: An Okinawa soba shop in central Naha picked in Mapple's Naha soba feature and profiled by Japan Travel.

F.n: C&C BREAKFAST OKINAWA (シーアンドシー ブレックファスト オキナワ)
F.w: A breakfast café a minute off Kokusai-dōri built around 'a delicious breakfast while traveling' — açaí bowls, pancakes and eggs Benedict. Ryukyu Shimpo highlighted its sweet-salty bacon-and-waffle combination.

F.n: Min'yō Stage Utahime, Kokusai-dōri (民謡ステージ歌姫)
F.w: A live Okinawan folk-song (min'yō) izakaya on Kokusai-dōri owned by Yoriko Ganeko, the singer known as 'Okinawa's songstress', with five stages a night. Food is the classic canon — gōyā champurū, rafute, fried gurukun — with Orion beer and three-year kusu awamori.

F.n: Chuko Awamori Distillery — Chuko-gura (忠孝酒造 忠孝蔵)
F.w: Founded in Tomigusuku in 1949 (as Tomigusuku Distillery); runs free ~1-hour tours of its distillery, kiln-fired pottery workshop and kusu cellars ending with a tasting of about ten awamori. Ten minutes' drive from Naha Airport.

F.n: Itoman Gyomin Shokudō (糸満漁民食堂)
F.w: Fish restaurant in the fishing town of Itoman, opened in 2013 in a building of stacked Ryūkyū limestone that won a Good Design Award and JCD Design Award. Its signature is the day's local fish butter-grilled until crisp outside and tender within.

F.n: Seifuku Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (請福酒造)
F.w: Ishigaki awamori maker founded in 1949, with a direct shop where the whole Seifuku range can be tasted and free ~15-minute factory tours at set times, no booking needed.

F.n: Yaesen Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (八重泉酒造)
F.w: Founded in 1955; the factory shop shows a 15-minute film of the distilling process and runs a tasting counter with shop-only bottles. Three Yaesen awamori won awards at a UK spirits competition (Ryukyu Shimpo).

F.n: Takamine Shuzōsho awamori distillery, Kabira (高嶺酒造所)
F.w: Small distillery beside Kabira Park making 'Omoto' awamori by hand — one of the few still using direct-fire (jika-bi) distillation; the process is visible through glass and tastings are offered.

F.n: Yakiniku Takesan-tei, Ishigaki (焼肉 たけさん亭)
F.w: Ishigaki-beef yakiniku whose owner holds cattle-auction buying rights and buys whole A4–A5 animals, so rarer cuts appear on the menu. Dinner only (closed Tue).

F.n: Yakiniku Kingyū, Ishigaki (焼肉 金牛)
F.w: Run by an Ishigaki family that has raised wagyu on the island for over 120 years; serves only its own Ishigaki beef, raised ~30 months and aged. Dinner only (closed Thu).

F.n: Taragawa awamori distillery, Miyako (多良川)
F.w: Maker of the long-selling 'Taragawa' awamori, brewed with spring water; free 40-minute tours of the plant and its cave storehouse run three times a day (closed Sun).

F.n: Yukishio Museum, Miyako (雪塩ミュージアム)
F.w: Showroom of the 'Yukishio' salt works, which makes powder-fine salt from limestone-filtered underground seawater; free guided looks at the production line, and the shop's Yukishio soft-serve is the draw.

F.n: Maeda Shokudō, Ōgimi (前田食堂)
F.w: Yanbaru noodle shop founded in 1972, on the way to Hiji Falls and Mt Yonaha; its signature gyūniku soba piles pepper-fried beef and bean sprouts on thin noodles, and weekend queues are the norm. Closes when the broth runs out.

F.n: Shima-buta Shichirin-yaki Manmi, Motobu (島豚七輪焼 満味)
F.w: Reservation-essential grill house for Yanbaru island pork descended from agu: cuts and offal grilled over individual charcoal shichirin, with rare pork tongue and a horumon fried rice to finish. Dinner only (closed Sun–Mon).

F.n: Okinawa Ryōri Maruoki Shōten, Nago (沖縄料理 丸沖商店)
F.w: Nago restaurant certified under Okinawa Prefecture's 'shop where you can taste Ryūkyū cuisine' scheme; known for its agu-pork shabu-shabu course.

F.n: Kumejima no Kumesen distillery, Kume Island (久米島の久米仙)
F.w: Kume Island's best-known awamori house: a video tour of the process and free tastings from light everyday awamori to rich aged kusu, including the island-only 'Kumishima' 3-year kusu (closed Sun & holidays).

F.n: KOURI SHRIMP, Kouri Island (古宇利島 KOURI SHRIMP)
F.w: Kouri Island's garlic-shrimp stand serving Hawaiian-style shrimp plates; Stars and Stripes notes it has opened a new shop on the island.

F.n: Pork Tamago Onigiri Honten, Makishi (ポークたまごおにぎり本店)
F.w: The flagship of the 'Pōtama' shop that turned Okinawa's pork-and-egg onigiri into a takeaway icon; each one is pressed to order so the rice is hot and the egg fluffy. Opens early (7:00) for breakfast, closed Wednesdays.

F.n: Fujiya Tomari Honten (富士家 泊本店)
F.w: The name many Okinawans give first for zenzai: fluffy shaved ice frozen from the bean-cooking syrup so it never dilutes, heaped over sweet kintoki beans. Open daily, later hours in summer.

F.n: Tomari Iyumachi Fish Market (泊いゆまち)
F.w: The Okinawa fisheries co-op's market by Tomari Port, where about 70 percent of the catch sold is tuna, delivered unfrozen the day it is landed. Stalls sell sashimi, seafood bowls, shellfish and mozuku to eat on the upstairs terrace.

F.n: Kokusai-dōri Yatai-mura (国際通り屋台村)
F.w: A food-stall village opened in 2015 just off Kokusai-dōri, with more than 20 counter stalls cooking Okinawan and island dishes from local ingredients — gurukun and parrotfish sushi, Agu pork dumplings, Ishigaki beef — from 11:00. A central stage hosts island songs and dances.

F.n: Arakaki Kashiten, Shuri Samukawa (新垣菓子店 首里寒川店)
F.w: A confectioner founded in 1932 by descendants of a cook to the Ryūkyū royal court, making chinsukō and other traditional Ryūkyū sweets at its Shuri shop.

F.n: Ryūkyū Ryōri Nuchigafū (琉球料理 ぬちがふぅ)
F.ad: Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa (hilltop off the southern end of Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri)
F.w: An elegant hilltop restaurant above the southern end of Tsuboya pottery street that Lonely Planet singles out for a memorable dinner of Ryūkyū cuisine. It is on Okinawa Prefecture's certified list of restaurants serving authentic Ryūkyū cuisine.

F.n: Kamimura Distillery Kūsu-gura (神村酒造 古酒蔵)
F.w: Awamori distillery founded in 1882 (originally in Naha's Shikina/Hantagawa), maker of Danryū — the 1968 cask-aged awamori credited with reviving post-war demand — and Shurei. Free ~40-minute tours (20 min distillery, 20 min tasting) by reservation, plus a direct shop and kūsu storage service.

F.n: Mihama Shokudō, Chatan (みはま食堂)
F.w: Local shokudō by Chatan's Mihama known for hone-jiru — pork backbones and tofu simmered in a kombu broth and eaten by hand — and hone-soba heaped with bone-in sōki; both often sell out early.

F.n: Sanchōme no Shima Soba-ya, Ginowan (3丁目の島そば屋)
F.ad: 3-10-1 Kakazu, Ginowan, Okinawa, Japan (White Papillon Sato 101)
F.w: Newer Ginowan soba shop picked among the eight best soba shops of central Okinawa in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers; Okinawa TV's Okitive praised its noodles, soup and toppings, notably the uneven mix of three noodle cuts.

F.n: Tacos-ya Chatan (タコス屋 北谷店)
F.ad: 1-5 Miyagi, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan (near the Sunabe Seawall)
F.w: Small taco shop on a backstreet near the Sunabe Seawall that has fed locals and visitors for about 35 years; it still fries its house-made shells to order for a chewy-crisp texture, and its Tacos-ya Plate piles tacos, taco rice, onion rings and fries on one plate.

F.n: Emi no Mise, Ōgimi (笑味の店)
F.w: Opened in 1990 by Kinjō Shōko to pass on the food culture of Ōgimi, the 'longevity village'; a farm restaurant whose reservation-only chōju-zen longevity set is built on seasonal island vegetables she grows herself. Her book of Yanbaru grandmothers' kitchen wisdom was published in 2023 (Ryukyu Shimpo).

F.n: Okashi Goten Onna (御菓子御殿 恩納店)
F.ad: Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (coastal Route 58; red-gated palace-style shop)
F.w: The red-gated seaside flagship of the confectioner behind the 'original' beni-imo tart, made from 100% Okinawan purple sweet potato from contracted farmers with no preservatives or colouring; the baking line is visible through glass and a reservation-only tart-making class runs here.

F.n: Mozuku Soba Kunnatu, Nanjō (もずくそばの店 くんなとぅ)
F.w: Facing Ōjima, a mozuku-farming centre, this shop kneads JAS-organic mozuku into its own soba noodles and serves them in a light bonito broth with tempura fried to order.

F.n: Seaside Drive-In, Onna (シーサイドドライブイン)
F.ad: Nakadomari, Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (Route 58, seaside)
F.w: Opened in 1967 under US administration and kept in its original style, neon signs and all; the signature creamy pork-bone soup is a take-out ritual for west-coast beach days, and a 24-hour take-out counter sells burgers, shaved ice and sides.

F.n: Yamakawa Shuzō awamori distillery, Motobu (山川酒造)
F.w: Motobu distillery founded in 1946 that makes awamori and long-aged kusu with Motobu spring water; cellar tours show rows of 50-year-old kusu jars and end with tastings that include 20-year-old kusu. Ryukyu Shimpo has reviewed its jar-aged 2011 vintage.

F.n: Kin Shōnyūdō cave awamori cellar — Ryū no Kura, Kin (金武鍾乳洞 古酒蔵 龍の蔵)
F.w: Since 1988 Kin Shuzō has aged its 'Ryū' awamori in a 270 m limestone cave held at a constant 18°C — billed as Japan's first cave kusu cellar — where over 14,000 bottles sit, many of them visitors' bottle-keeps for 5, 12 or 20 years; guided cave tours run three times a day.

F.n: Hateruma Shuzōsho — Awanami distillery, Hateruma Island (波照間酒造所)
F.ad: Hateruma Island, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: The only distillery on Hateruma, Japan's southernmost inhabited island, making Awanami — the so-called 'phantom awamori' that sells out within minutes; bottles and Awanami goods are sold at the distillery shop.

F.n: Sakimoto Shuzōsho — hanazake distillery, Yonaguni (崎元酒造所)
F.w: Yonaguni's oldest distillery, still firing a traditional direct-fire pot still by hand; maker of the awamori 'Yonaguni' and of hanazake, the 60% first-run spirit that only Yonaguni is permitted to make. Distillery shop sells brewery-only bottles.

F.n: Pengin Shokudō, Ishigaki (辺銀食堂)
F.ad: Ishigaki city centre (7 min walk from Ishigaki bus terminal), Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan
F.w: Birthplace of Ishigaki-jima rāyu, the hand-made island-salt-and-chilli oil that started Japan's 'edible rāyu' boom; at lunch the house order is jājan-suba (thick noodles with spicy miso), served until sold out.

F.n: Akashi Shokudō, Ishigaki (明石食堂)
F.ad: 360 Ihara, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan (Akashi area, north Ishigaki)
F.w: Old-guard north-Ishigaki shokudō about 40 minutes' drive from town, with queues before opening for its soft-bone sōki Yaeyama soba — clean pork-bone broth over round straight noodles. Ranked No.1 in a 2019 Okinawa-soba ranking reported by Ryukyu Shimpo.

F.n: Arakaki Shokudō, Ishigaki — CLOSED (新垣食堂)
F.w: Ihara shokudō whose beef-broth soba, made with beef from the family's own ranch, won the original-soup division of the first Yaeyama Soba Championship. CLOSED: it shut on 27 November after 35 years (Yaeyama Mainichi).

F.n: Kuninaka Shokudō, Miyako (くになか食堂)
F.w: Locals' Miyako-soba shokudō in Miyakojima city, picked in Rurubu's eight best Miyako soba and in Mapple's Miyako dining list.

F.n: Tokuyama Shuzō awamori distillery, Irabu Island (渡久山酒造)
F.w: Compact Irabu Island awamori distillery run by the third-generation Tokuyama couple, still distilling by traditional methods; shop open 10:00-16:00 weekdays. One of three Miyako distilleries showcased at the first Shima-zake Festa (2018).

F.n: Sakana-dokoro Shiken-bara, Miyako (肴処 志堅原)
F.w: Constantly-full izakaya on Hirara's Nishizato-dōri izakaya strip, serving fresh fish from the waters around Miyako as sashimi and salt-simmered mās-ni, with island awamori.

F.n: Kumejima Soba-dokoro Yan-kō, Kume Island (久米島そば処 やん小～)
F.w: Soba shop in an old Ryūkyū-style house making hand-cut noodles with Kume's deep-sea water; the signature is a rare miso-flavoured soba piled with island-grown bean sprouts. Lunch only (11:30-13:30), closed Sundays.

F.n: Yonejima Shuzō awamori distillery, Kume Island (米島酒造)
F.w: Small Kume Island distillery founded by Tabata Ryōtoku, who was drawn by the island's abundant water and varied geology; shop open 10-12 and 14-17, closed Sundays.

F.n: Fruit Parlour Kōrakuen, Ishigaki (光楽園)
F.w: Fruit parlour popular with both locals and visitors on Ishigaki, with a long line-up of chilled sweets built on tropical island fruit; featured in its own Rurubu piece and in Mapple's Ishigaki sweets round-up.

F.n: How Tree Gelato, Ishigaki (ハウトゥリージェラート)
F.w: Specialist in cold-plate marble ice cream mixing fresh fruit from the owners' own farm with Ishigaki Island milk; seasonal (Feb-Nov).

F.n: Blue Turtle, Irabu Island (ブルー タートル)
F.ad: Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan (facing Toguchi-no-hama beach)
F.w: White sea-view café-restaurant on Irabu Island right in front of Toguchi-no-hama, one of Irabu's finest beaches; known for hamburg steak and for ice cream served over hidden layers of coloured shaved ice.
